handoff.summary: Implemented per-app and name-allocation locks in src/platform/lock.ts and cross-app declared-port checks in src/registry/ports.ts. Locks record pid and start time, publish atomically, fail immediately with exit 6 naming the holder, reclaim dead-pid or malformed locks, and release on every throw path. Ports reject privileged/out-of-range values with exit 1 and duplicate declarations with exit 6 regardless of bind address. Typecheck, lint, build, the 26 focused tests, and the full 263-test suite pass.
decisions: App lock file is <appDir>/.lock; the short-lived allocation lock is <appsDir>/.<name>.allocation.lock, a plain file the registry listing ignores.

Lock documents are {schemaVersion, pid, startedAt, operation, app, token} with mode 0600, written to a same-directory temp file and hard-linked into place so another process never observes a partial lock.
A live holder raises ConflictError LOCK_HELD (exit 6) that names the pid, operation, app, and start time; a lock whose pid is dead or whose document is unparseable is reclaimed.
Stale reclamation renames the lock to a unique quarantine path and verifies the bytes are unchanged before deleting, so it cannot remove a lock a third process just acquired.
Release verifies the acquisition token first, so a process never deletes a lock another holder replaced; withAppLock and withAllocationLock release in finally.
Port conflicts compare equality only and never bind addresses; the requesting app's own claim is skipped when options.app is supplied so updates can keep their port.

Missing app directory, unreadable lock file, and unwritable lock location are PrerequisiteError exit 2 (LOCK_DIRECTORY_MISSING, LOCK_UNREADABLE, LOCK_NOT_WRITABLE); contention is exit 6. No new error classes were invented.
interfaces: LockAcquireOptions {app?, operation?, pid?, clock?, isProcessAlive?, maxReclaimAttempts?}
warnings: Stale detection uses pid liveness only; a reused pid could keep an abandoned lock until that unrelated process exits. startedAt is recorded for diagnostics but not compared against /proc start time.
App locks are strictly non-blocking, matching REG-FR-05's immediate exit-6 rule; callers that want to wait must retry themselves.
The allocation lock is created in apps/ as a hidden plain file; Registry.list ignores plain files, so it cannot appear as a broken app.
